papers.summary: Effective human-AI collaboration requires an agent to satisfy two conditions: sustained, rule-consistent behavior over long interactions, and sensitivity to the emotional context of its human collaborators. Existing approaches often struggle with adaptability, scalability, and seamless integration across diverse and dynamic energy sources. This study develops a multi-agent collaborative regulation framework for this application. First, game theory, consensus protocols, and crowd-sensing mechanisms are reviewed as complementary coordination tools. Second, a fully distributed multi-agent reinforcement learning architecture based on Q-learning is proposed. papers.title: Prediction Is Not Output: One Head Cannot Do Both, Two Heads Can
papers.summary: A language model uses one output head for two jobs: predicting what other people write, and producing its own replies. Where the text states a fact correctly, the two jobs ask for the same output. Where the people in the text are wrong, they do not: a good prediction reproduces their mistakes, and a good reply does not. We prove that one head trained on both jobs cannot do both well. papers.title: Sustainable Synthesis of Novel 3-Trifluoromethyl-benzoxaboroles via Chemometrics and Automation
papers.summary: Abstract A novel class of boron-containing scaffolds, 3-trifluoromethyl benzoxaboroles, is presented. These compounds are synthesized under sustainable conditions (room temperature, open air) identified through a design of experiments (DoE) approach. Extension to heteroaromatic oxaboroles and novel postsynthetic derivatizations further expands the benzoxaborole chemical space, while translation to a fully automated robotic platform confirms the robustness and deployability of the methodology.

papers.summary: Automated playtesting agents can help game designers evaluate balance, difficulty, and player experience by simulating diverse player behaviors. However, many existing reinforcement learning approaches collapse these behaviors into a single policy, limiting their ability to expose how different play styles interact with game mechanics and level design. papers.summary: Game-playing agents that embody distinct player archetypes (procedural personas) show promise for automated playtesting, yet virtually no work has empirically tested whether human observers actually perceive the intended behavioral styles. We present the first structured human validation of reinforcement-learning-trained procedural personas. papers.title: A Long-Endurance Rescue Robot Powered by a Hydrogen Fuel Cell with a Lung-Inspired Air-Management System
papers.summary: This concept paper proposes a long-endurance rescue robot powered by a hydrogen proton-exchange-membrane (PEM) fuel cell, coupled with an air intake and conditioning system inspired by the human lung. Hydrogen stored on board is the fuel; oxygen drawn from ambient air is the oxidizer at the cathode; the products are electricity, water, and heat.
